method.inputTokens: the sum of inputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens over every model in modelUsage of the --output-format json result (usage.input_tokens + usage.cache_creation_input_tokens + usage.cache_read_input_tokens when there is no modelUsage); the page shows this. A run whose top-level usage differs also keeps usageInputTokens.
method.outputTokens: the sum of outputTokens over every model in modelUsage (usage.output_tokens when there is none); the page shows this. A run whose top-level usage differs also keeps usageOutputTokens.
method.usageByModel: each model's inputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens, outputTokens, costUSD from modelUsage, as reported
method.toolCalls: the distinct toolUseId values on "tool_dispatch_start" lines in the --debug-file log; null when the session took more than one turn and the log has no such line, and such runs are left out of the tool-call figures

questions.question: May I add a new top-level folder to the tree in `refs/chamoji/memory`?
questions.key: No: the layout is fixed until a new format gets its own ref or a version bump, because older clients drop what they don't know.

questions.question: Should `chamoji init` set `remote.origin.push` so a plain `git push` also pushes memory?
questions.key: No: it must not set it, and the fetch refspec must be a wildcard, or plain push, fetch and pull break.

questions.question: Why does the command in the Claude Code hook entries end in `|| true`?
questions.key: Claude Code reads exit 2 as a block; a denial is JSON on stdout with exit 0 and still gets through.

questions.question: Can I add the official MCP SDK as a dependency for `chamoji mcp`?
questions.key: No: it would double chamoji's install for five methods.

questions.question: Why does `chamoji why` blame the working copy and not HEAD?
questions.key: So line numbers match the editor, and an edited line is reported as uncommitted.

Claude Code treats a hook exit code of 2 as a block, so ending both command forms with `|| true` forces a successful exit and a failing hook can't stop the agent. A real denial is still delivered as JSON on stdout with exit 0, so it gets through. I relied on constraint c-f3ea2f10 (commit 800050c), which fits c-5833401c (commit 6617b21): the hook must always exit 0.

It blames the working copy so that line numbers match what you see in the editor. An edited but uncommitted line is then reported as uncommitted, not blamed on an older commit. This is constraint `c-7a4d905c` from commit `2fd0da6` ("✨ Add chamoji why to explain a line").

It's deliberate. In `packages/core/src/blame.ts:49-50`, `blameLine` runs `git blame` with no revision argument, so it blames the working copy. The comment there says this keeps line numbers matching what an editor shows, and a line you haven't committed yet comes back as `uncommitted` instead of being blamed on the wrong commit (`blame.ts:61`). The readme's `why` section (`readme.md:191`) says the same. I didn't look through git history for the commit that introduced this choice, so I can't name one.

`chamoji why` runs `git blame` with no revision argument, which blames the working copy (`packages/core/src/blame.ts:49`). That way the line numbers you give match the file you have open, and a line you haven't committed yet comes back as `uncommitted` instead of being pinned on an older commit. The design was introduced in commit `2fd0da6` ("Add chamoji why to explain a line") and is documented in `readme.md:191`. I didn't find a written rationale beyond the code comments and readme, so the "why" above is inferred from them.

It blames the working copy so that line numbers match what you see in your editor. An edited but uncommitted line is then reported as uncommitted, not blamed on an older commit. This is constraint `c-7a4d905c`, recorded in commit `2fd0da6` ("✨ Add chamoji why to explain a line").

`chamoji why` takes a `file:line` location, and that location's line number comes from what the user sees in their editor. `blameLine` in `packages/core/src/blame.ts:49-52` runs `git blame` with no revision for that reason (the comment there says so). Blaming HEAD would shift the line numbers whenever there are uncommitted edits. Leaving out the revision also lets an uncommitted line come back as the all-zero hash, which the code reports as `{kind: 'uncommitted'}` instead of naming a commit. The function was added in commit `2fd0da6` ("✨ Add chamoji why to explain a line"), and the readme (line 191) documents the behavior.
